articles.title: Vizhinjam to get India's first outer service port modelled on UAE's Fujairah
articles.content: Rakesh K Nair Last Updated: 23 November 2026, 11:01 AM IST 2 min Share Follow us on Located close to an international shipping route, the proposed outer port at Vizhinjam will offer a range of services to vessels passing through the route ❎ Vizhinjam International Seaport Thiruvananthapuram: Vizhinjam is set to get an outer port modelled on Fujairah in the UAE as part of Mission Samudra, a government initiative aimed at transforming Kerala into a major port hub. The project will be implemented by developing the old port into a service harbour. To advertise here, Contact Us Located close to an international shipping route, the proposed outer port at Vizhinjam will offer a range of services to vessels passing through the route. These will include engineering services such as repairs and maintenance, spare parts supply, fuel (bunkering) and crew changes. The old port will be developed to accommodate large boats and small ships. Earlier, the government had proposed setting up an outer harbour in the open sea in collaboration with the Indian Navy. The Navy's cooperation is also expected to be sought for the project. The Fujairah offshore anchorage facility provides bunkering and other services to cargo vessels travelling through the Strait of Hormuz. Currently, no port in India offers such a range of services. The project is expected to attract investment and generate employment without requiring large-scale land acquisition. The government has decided to appoint an agency to study the project's environmental and economic feasibility. The first phase of Mission Samudra aims to develop four ports under the Kerala Maritime Board — Vizhinjam, Kollam, Beypore and Azhikkal. articles.title: When will Indians fly to space ? ISRO's Gaganyaan mission may face another launch delay
articles.content: Business News Science News When will Indians fly to space? ISRO's Gaganyaan mission may face another launch delay When will Indians fly to space? ISRO's Gaganyaan mission may face another launch delay ISRO's first unmanned Gaganyaan flight may be postponed to February 2027 as technical checks continue. The delay underscores the agency's focus on safety before sending Indian astronauts into space. Advertisement Share: The Gaganyaan mission was approved in January 2019, with India’s first human spaceflight initially targeted for May 2022. Business Today Desk Nov 23, 2026, Updated Nov 23, 2026 7:00 AM IST Subscribe to Notifications India’s long wait for its first human spaceflight mission may grow longer, with the first unmanned Gaganyaan flight now expected to launch no earlier than February 2027. The mission was previously scheduled for December 2026. Senior Indian Space Research Organisation officials told Aaj Tak that technical checks, additional simulations and system tests could delay the launch. About 80% of the work has been completed, but essential procedures must be finished before the spacecraft and launch vehicle are cleared for flight. The G1 mission will carry ISRO’s humanoid robot Vyommitra and test key systems required before Indian astronauts can be sent into space. Advertisement Read More Related Articles 'Russia stood by India': ISRO chief V Narayanan recalls Moscow's role in space journey ISRO's Aditya-L1 detects uneven solar eruption, could improve space weather forecasts Why Gaganyaan’s first unmanned flight may be delayed Officials from the Human Space Flight Centre and the U R Rao Satellite Centre said ISRO was focused on ensuring complete safety as Gaganyaan would be India’s first demonstration of human spaceflight capability. ISRO Chairman Dr V Narayanan had earlier indicated that the first unmanned Gaganyaan mission would be included in the 2026 launch schedule. Following the successful launch of GSLV-F17 with EOS-05 in September, he said six more launches were planned during the year, including NVS-03 and Gaganyaan’s first unmanned flight. Narayanan said nearly 8,000 tests had been completed for the mission. He added that protecting human life was paramount in this mission compared with other satellite missions. Work on the crew escape system had progressed, while the environmental control and safety systems were also at advanced stages. Advertisement How Gaganyaan’s launch timeline changed The Gaganyaan mission was approved in January 2019, with India’s first human spaceflight initially targeted for May 2022. The plan envisaged two unmanned missions before the human spaceflight. The COVID-19 pandemic disrupted hardware manufacturing and supply chains, forcing the launch schedule to be revised. By August 2025, the first unmanned mission was scheduled for the last quarter of 2025. The target was later moved to the last quarter of 2026. The scope of the mission was also expanded in October 2024 from three flights to eight. Vyommitra to fly on Gaganyaan’s G1 mission The first unmanned flight, G1, will carry ISRO’s humanoid robot Vyommitra.
